title: The Leeward Wreck
premise: Tamsin Brightwater, a debt-ridden storm chaser hiding in a coastal village, discovers a tide-revealed sea cave containing the wreck of the Leeward—a lost ship whose manifest could clear his debts or bury him. Pursued by the creditors who financed his last expedition, he must cross the mountains ahead of the early snows with the evidence, guided by a local woman whose grandfather died aboard the Leeward. Betrayal, a brutal storm, and a final reckoning force Tamsin to choose between the fortune that would free him and the truth that would honor the dead. He chooses truth, trading his windfall for the wreck's rightful inheritance, and ends the book poorer, freer, and finally visible.
about_author: Kestrel Villalobos is the pen name of a former marine salvage surveyor who spent a decade mapping shipwrecks along storm-battered coastlines before turning to fiction. Their adventure novels are known for ruthless weather, moral arithmetic, and characters who learn that survival is a debt everyone eventually pays.

chapters.title: The Debt of Optimists
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Hiding in the fishing village of Greyhaven, Tamsin dodges letters from the Vane Syndicate, the creditors who funded his last doomed expedition. A violent gale wrecks his gear and his last excuse to stay. Emotional beat: cornered exhaustion, the sense that running has become his whole identity.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gives Back
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. After an extreme spring tide, Tamsin explores a newly exposed sea cave and finds the Leeward, a legendary wreck, remarkably preserved, with a sealed manifest chest. He pockets one document before the cave floods. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as he realizes what he's holding.

chapters.title: The Granddaughter of the Leeward
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren Corvane, a ferry pilot whose grandfather died aboard the Leeward, catches Tamsin photographing charts and confronts him. Reluctantly, they form an uneasy alliance: the manifest proves her family was cheated of salvage rights decades ago. Emotional beat: wary trust forged over shared grievance.

chapters.title: Men Who Smile Like Weather
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The Vane Syndicate arrives in Greyhaven, charming and menacing, having learned of the cave. They offer to forgive Tamsin's debt in exchange for the manifest—and make it clear refusal has a price. Emotional beat: the seductive relief of surrender versus the shame of it.

chapters.title: Dry Season, Closing Fast
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. With the mountain pass closing in weeks and the Syndicate's watchers everywhere, Maren and Tamsin plan a crossing with the manifest, her grandfather's journal, and a borrowed plane that can only go so far. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Long Ascent
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The crossing begins; a Syndicate tracker shadows them, and Tamsin's old injury flares on the scree. Maren saves his life, cementing their bond but deepening his guilt over what the manifest might cost her family. Emotional beat: dependence he never wanted and can't deny.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Early snows catch them at a shelter where the tracker corners them. Tamsin talks his way into a standoff, then betrays their route to the tracker in exchange for Maren's safe passage—lying to her face. Emotional beat: the terrible arithmetic of loyalty versus survival.

chapters.title: What He Owes the Dead
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Alone with the manifest, Tamsin reads his grandfather's name among the Leeward's investors—his debt is inherited, not earned. The revelation reframes everything. Emotional beat: grief and fury, and the first honest look at who he's become.

chapters.title: The Reckoning at Vane House
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren, having discovered the betrayal, races ahead and reaches the Syndicate first. Tamsin arrives to find her holding them to their own contract with the manifest as leverage. In the climax, Tamsin publicly surrenders the manifest as evidence, voiding his debt and exposing the Syndicate's fraud. Emotional beat: cathartic confrontation, truth as the only currency left.

chapters.title: Leeward
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Weeks later: the Syndicate is under investigation, the Corvane family's salvage rights restored, and Tamsin—penniless but unowned—signs on to Maren's survey of the wreck. The cave closes with the tides, keeping its secrets. Emotional beat: quiet peace; visibility, at last, as a choice.
